final.rationale:
LEAD WITH THIS WHEN PRESENTING: every room frame in this round is the in-game camera (pitch 0.46, distance 13.4). From that camera the oculus is never in frame. It is implied by its beam entering at the top edge (about screen x 1265). Only view-up-not-in-game shows it, and that view is labelled as one the game cannot show.

FREE WORK ALREADY DONE (0 credits). The critique asked for a to-scale plan, a to-scale section and a HUD check before any credits are spent. All three exist now, in art/reference/concepts/rooms-fresh/travertine-layout/:
- blockout-camera.png and blockout-camera-cascade.png: Blender massing renders taken from the exact game camera, with flat colour-coded clay.
- blockout-camera-hud.png: the HUD overlay, plus the computed pool points and focus spot.
- plan.png: to scale, with hotspots, laid-object spots, lanterns, today's capacity ovals and the camera frustum.
- section.png: to scale, from the HubCity constants.

The scripts are in the scratchpad (C:\Users\jrpry\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\B--Projects-Atrium-custom\a2dd308f-2277-4dfa-ab31-57a98c64c701\scratchpad\travertine\):
- layout.py: the shared numbers.
- blockout_flat.py: the Blender render that was used.
- diagrams.py, then render_svgs.ps1: plan, section, and a HUD overlay for any image.
Run diagrams.py on every master and finish candidate and reject any that fails. Overlays of the three Travertine concepts are in the scratchpad's svg/ folder. They show each concept's upper-left mouth under the clock, title and tabs.

THE LAYOUT. These are the tested positions, nudged because the tested ovals overlapped in plan: the middle bowl would have hung up to 0.7 m over the bottom pool's back, where Hush-Moss grows. Pools are at full size (5.9 x 2.4 m).
- Top (Sunward, pool 0): water +1.5 at (2.4, -3.6), screen (1056, 342), seen at 21 deg.
- Middle (Spawning, pool 2): water 0 at (0, -1.2), screen (782, 532), 30 deg.
- Bottom (Shade, pool 1): water -1.5 at (-3.0, 1.1), screen (430, 726), 36 deg. Its laid-object spot is at (379, 784), clear of the caption and the satchel bar.
- One spare bowl (pool 3): water 0 at (6.4, -0.1), turned 90 deg, screen (1455, 704), 33 deg. It is clear of every hotspot. Pools 4 and up go in alcoves round the right wall, off the default frame, reached by tabs and focus. The room already has to extend there for focus close-ups.
- Mouth: x 0.5 to 1.9 on the back wall, sill +2.4, crown +4.0. Screen (926-1052, 73-213), clear of all HUD.
- Furniture is split. The druids' bag sits on the landing by the mouth, where Sanctum deliveries arrive (screen 803, 165). Ledger (3.8, -0.4), stool (2.7, 0.7) and crock (4.0, 1.45) share a 4.5 m ledge with no overlapping hotspots, at screen (1161, 530), (1015, 613) and (1166, 680). The crock is not at the front centre because that spot falls under the hover caption.

THE WORLD (section). The oculus sits in the scarp shelf at world (18.9, -1, -11.2), 2.4 m beyond the wall's outer face. The hub never shows it, so the hub needs no change. Room y 0 is world -7.5. From the hub's four steps, about 4.3 m more of stair (about 44 deg) runs down under the wall's footings, with the brook in a channel beside it.

CODE CHANGES THIS LAYOUT NEEDS (so nobody approves a 'no code' route that needs code):
1. Pool positions and yaw come from kit markers pool-0..n, replacing Slots. With a 90 deg yaw, pick the sign so the laid-object front faces -x, toward the camera.
2. The spill follows a kit-supplied runnel path (bypass), or runs by height (cascade). As coded today, a straight pool 0 to pool 1 ribbon would pour across the Spawning Pond.
3. The trickle starts at a mouth-brook marker instead of the crack at y 5.4.
4. The river is replaced by the outflow under the left arch.
5. The focus clamp (PoolsScene.cs:972) is lowered to about -2.
6. SunDir changes to about (0.43, 0.89, -0.14) to match the beam, which is an additive mesh.
7. Kit bowls with per-bowl parts replace the BuildBasin rims, so the hover rim and lift keep working.

STAGES.
- Stage 1, run now: five layout masters, 11.5 credits. Then the free HUD check. Then pick one master.
- Stage 2a, after the master pick: four finishes and one clay focus frame, 18 credits.
- Stage 2b, after the finish pick: everything else in the winning finish, 22 credits.
Total 51.5 credits, one GPT job.

MUST-FIXES APPLIED.
1. Keyframe A is gone from the round. It is the finish of the set-aside rooms-round paint-overs (pools-a), so using it would loop back to them. The 'match the hub' finish uses corner-a instead, the hub's current corner target (iteration-3-log.md:428-435). Until the finish is picked, the stage-2b shots carry Nano A as a provisional style reference, to be swapped for the winning image. Props, the kit and the grids run only after the pick, so nothing is paid for twice.
2. Masters. One Nano and the GPT run text-only. The GPT Travertine reference goes on the second Nano only, so its drift is visible. Two more Nano masters are added, built on the computed blockouts: the bypass route, and the brief's cascade (the critique's optional variant). Both have the same layout, so the water route is the only difference.
3. The section is drawn to scale for free. One Nano render is built on that drawing, and the second variant is cut.

SHOULD-FIXES.
- Applied: the critique's camera wording, colour-coded clay, near-equal 2.4:1 ovals, a spare bowl placed by calculation, split furniture, the engine's true start state in every finish, two 2K images per finish, one realism sample labelled as needing a renderer change, a build-honest finish, the Sun-Lens steam-in-beam case with frost on a cream lip, a cream-backed energy grid with an unlit identical lantern, the residents row replacing the engine-drawn primitives, the kit pieces corrected, no baked glow and no water in the props, and the night frame moved to 2b as exploratory.
- Kept against advice: the residents sheet keeps its clarity row. The finishes show only the 85% silt state, and clearing silt is the cozy loop's main tell.
- Cut rather than reframed: view-threshold. The masters show the mouth at game scale, and the section render shows the descent.
- Deferred: materials-travertine. Which surfaces need tiles is not known until the Blender blockout, and the existing post-pass makes tiles seamless.

CUT: view-plan (drawn instead), finish-painterly-gpt, view-threshold, the section's second variant and the materials sheet.

UPLOADS NEEDED: blockout-camera.png, blockout-camera-cascade.png, section.png, city-round/corner-a.jpg, city-round/night-a.jpg and textures/stoic-bark.png.

shots.title: Layout master, clay, text only (Nano)
shots.purpose: Stage 1. Nano's own reading of the layout brief with no image to copy. It is one of five candidate masters. Every stage-2 room frame repaints the chosen master, and it guides the Blender blockout. Run the free HUD overlay on it before choosing.
shots.prompt: Matte clay model of a full-size sinkhole grotto with terraced rimstone pools. Seen from the front and a little to the right, back wall nearly square-on, looking down about 25 degrees; no tabletop, no base, no depth-of-field blur. The room fills the frame edge to edge; walls rise out of the top of the frame, no sky, no ceiling. Three oval pools, each about 2.4 times as long as wide, nearly equal, the middle one slightly smaller, step down toward the viewer: top pool upper right of centre against the back wall, middle pool dead centre, bottom pool lower left. Near lips stay low, so every bed shows. A slanting sunbeam enters from the top right edge onto the top pool. High on the back wall above the top pool's left end, a round-headed cave mouth no taller than a door: worn steps leave its left half and become a stair of thick roots down the left wall; a small brook falls from its right half into the top pool. A narrow runnel carries the top pool's overflow left and down past the middle pool into the bottom pool, which drains under a low arch in the left wall. A bag beside the mouth. On a ledge right of the middle pool: reading stand, stool on a mat, lidded crock. Far right, a fourth pool-sized bowl, dry. Cream travertine, pale grey walls, blue-grey rock round the bottom pool, brown roots, flat pale-turquoise water, light grey props. No people, no text.

The bottom pool, deep in root shade, has been brightened against its setting: pale gold-green water with dappled light across its bed, three fish glowing faintly, one plump with eggs. The dry bowl on the right now holds clear teal water as a fourth pool, with its own small lantern on a stake and two new fish. Butter-yellow snails on the beds, never on the rims. Chunky fish, a ninth of a pool's length. No people, no text.

No sunbeam now: only a faint cool blue glow falls from the unseen opening high above onto the top pool, and the cave mouth is a dim blue doorway with one small warm lamp at the top of the steps beyond. problems.problem: Seven shots (both grids, the prop sheet, textures, tended, view-up and the kit, about 26 credits) default to keyframe A before the finish is chosen. Keyframe A is the style of the set-aside paint-overs: rooms-round/pools-a.jpg is already keyframe-A gouache at this camera, with stake lanterns, a stool on a mat, a crock and a bag. Finish A plus the keyframe-A state shots will recreate it, which is the affirmation loop the designer named. The fresh-takes round kept every keyframe out on purpose. Props, textures and the kit all depend on the finish, so if another finish wins they get paid for twice.
problems.fix: Re-stage the round. Stage 1: layout masters only, plus the free HUD-overlay check. Stage 2a: the finishes. Stage 2b runs after the finish is picked, with everything else in the winning finish: props, textures, kit, grids, tended, night and the section render. If anything has to run early, use the chosen Travertine images' own finish (Nano A/B) as the provisional style, not keyframe A.

problems.problem: The only reference is the GPT Travertine image, and its composition contradicts what the prompt asks for: sky opening top-centre, mouth upper-left, a big middle pool, and the top pool pouring straight into the middle one. In a composition shot, that is the worst case for Nano's leakage. layout-clay-gpt, given its own model's image, will mostly redraw it. Every stage-2 frame inherits whatever the master gets wrong.
problems.fix: Run one Nano variant and the GPT variant text-only, as the fresh-takes round did. Keep the reference on the second Nano variant only, so the drift is visible and comparable before a master is chosen.

problems.problem: 'From high above its open front-right corner ... like a dollhouse' invites a 45-degree tabletop miniature, with a base and tilt-shift blur. The game's yaw is only 0.3 rad (17 deg), so the back wall reads almost square-on. 'Flat clay colours' gives the repaint and the blockout no way to tell water from stone. Pool sizes are unstated, so the brief's 'widest middle pool' can creep back in.
problems.fix: Use: 'a full-size room seen from the front and a little to the right, back wall nearly square-on, looking down about 25 degrees; no tabletop, no base, no depth-of-field blur'. Colour-code the clay: cream travertine, blue-grey shade rock, brown roots, flat pale-turquoise water, neutral props. Add: 'three ovals about 2.4 times as long as wide, nearly equal, the middle one slightly smaller'. Apply the same edits to layout-clay-gpt.

problems.problem: The spare bowls. The back-left one, at about (587, 260), sits under the working card and just below the tab strip. A water plane there is seen at about 18 deg, under the 20-deg floor, and it is higher than the Sunward, which breaks the descending order. The right-wall one, at about (1395, 560), is about (5.9, 0.5, -1.6) in the room. Sized to hold the required 5.87 x 2.39 m oval, it overlaps the work ledge and runs under the top pool's right end. Unsized, Nano will draw small birdbaths that no pool can use.
problems.fix: Say every spare bowl is as large as the pools. Place them by calculation: water seen at 20 deg or more, outside screen x < 640, clear of the ledge hotspots, which probably means past x 6 on the right, where the room must extend for focus close-ups anyway. Or show one spare and leave its placement to the blockout's pool markers.

problems.problem: The ledge holds four props within screen x 1020-1320, about 2.6 m at that depth (about 115 px/m). Their hotspots alone add up to about 4.7 m wide (crock 1.75, bag 1.1, ledger 1.05, stool 0.76), so the click boxes overlap and resolve to whichever is nearer.
problems.fix: Make the ledge about 6 m (screen x about 900-1550). Or split the furniture: ledger and stool on the ledge, the crock between the middle and bottom pools or at the foot of the stair, and the druids' bag near the mouth, where Sanctum deliveries arrive.

problems.problem: The heights contradict the hub. Just beyond the wall's outer face the ground is the scarp shelf at y -1 (HubCity.cs:424), and the hub mouth has only four shallow steps (about 0.2 m). A 'short tunnel' therefore leaves no room for a well 'about three storeys deep' with an oculus 'high above'. And with SunDir (0.15, 0.85, -0.5), a beam that lands on the back terrace has to come from an oculus over or behind the back wall, near the wall's footprint. An image model will paint a plausible section that quietly settles all of this wrongly, and the section is meant to be a build guide. Two variants double the cost.
problems.fix: First draw the section to scale for free (matplotlib or SVG) from the HubCity constants and the tested layout: courtyard 0, shelf -1, wall x 12.9-16.5, gate crown 7.2, gallery about 4, terraces +1.5/0/-1.5, frame top at the back wall about 4.7. Decide the descent (about 4-6 m of stair under the wall) or a courtyard well-head. Then, if a picture is still wanted, make one Nano render with that drawing as its structure reference. Cut the second variant.

problems.problem: The rationale says the runnel bypass means 'the spill still runs pool 0 to pool 1 as the code does'. It doesn't. PoolsScene.cs:207-214 draws a straight ribbon from pool 0's lip toward pool 1's centre. From (2.4, 1.5, -3.6) to (-2.9, -1.5, 0.4), that line passes through the middle pool's centre at (-0.3, 0, -1.0), so as coded the spill pours straight across the Spawning Pond.
problems.fix: Next to the master, list the code change: a spill path from kit markers, or a runnel the kit supplies. Then the designer isn't approving a 'no code change' route that needs code.

problems.problem: All four finish prompts say 'water as the game begins', but the water they describe doesn't match the engine. Start energy is base plus emissions. Sunward is Light +3 / Heat +1, because each Yellow-backed Snail emits +1 Light, so it shows the glow above the surface (Light 2 or more) and a bright dappled bed even under 85% silt. Shade is Light -3 / Heat -1 because Hush-Moss emits -1, and WaterColours makes that indigo-slate, not 'green-slate'. Spawning is Light +1. The prompts leave out the two butter-shelled snails, the Hush-Moss and the Sunward glow. The finishes are justified as 'the player's real first view', and they aren't.
problems.fix: In all four finish prompts, describe the engine's start state: the Sunward silted olive-jade with a soft glow over it and two butter-yellow snails on the bed; the Shade indigo-slate with dark moss along the back of its bed; the Spawning near-teal with its glowing reed. Or record 'green-slate' as a decision to change the shader.

problems.problem: The finish comparison is one 4K image per finish, so per-image luck decides the finish: layout drift, or Nano A's in-frame oculus leaking in through the style reference. Both painterly variants ask for 'no ink outlines', which this renderer can't produce: every mesh gets an inverted-hull outline, and there are flat toon bands, no shadows and no reflections. Keyframe A is also not the hub's current target: the designer's later picks (corner-a, wide-a, night-a) are what the hub build follows.
problems.fix: Run two images per finish at 2K for the same credits. Keep one realism sample (Nano), labelled as needing a renderer change. Give Finish A corner-a as its style reference, or add corner-a alongside keyframe A. Add a build-honest finish (see missing shots).

problems.problem: It tests only the contradiction case. The most likely mid-game state is the Sun-Lens laid in the Sunward Basin: +2/+1 on top of Light 3 / Heat 1 gives Light 5 / Heat 2, with steam rising inside the noon beam. That is exactly where the GPT concept lost its steam, and no shot tests it.
problems.fix: Have the top pool steam inside the beam; darken its water too if the contradiction test is kept. Test frost on a cream lip on the newly filled fourth bowl or the middle pool, and keep the bottom pool bright. Judge fish readability on the image scaled down to 1600x900.

problems.problem: All nine panels sit against a dark mossy wall, the case where steam and frost read easily. So the grid can't show the risks the requirements name: steam against the beam or pale stone, and frost on cream. Every panel also has a lantern whose warm light will read as Heat. 4K is more than ~900 px panels need.
problems.fix: Use a cream travertine backdrop, with the noon beam crossing the top-row (hot) panels. Make the lantern unlit, or identical in every panel. Run at 2K.

problems.problem: The bottom row paints things the engine draws itself: the soak ring of 16 dots (Nano can't count them reliably) and the crystal, orb, jar and pebble primitives. The clarity row repeats the finishes' start state. Meanwhile the starting plants and snails appear in no shot.
problems.fix: Replace those panels with Hush-Moss along the back of the bed, the Lantern Reed's glowing tip, butter-shelled Yellow-backed Snails grazing the bed, and sun-motes vs frost-motes. Run at 2K.

problems.problem: It asks for an oculus rim, which is never in frame, so building it is wasted. It asks for a frost-crusted lip, but frost is live state (Heat -2 or less, PoolsScene.cs:1280), so baking it in breaks 'live state beats architecture'. It leaves out pieces the build needs: each bowl as its own part, so the hover rim and lift still work; the mouth's sill with steps and brook; the low outflow arch; a landing for the root stair.
problems.fix: Drop the oculus rim and the frost crust. Add those pieces, including one dry bowl large enough for the full oval. Run it after the finish is picked.

problems.problem: 'A faint glow at its mouth' on the bag bakes in a live state: the mouth glows only while something waits inside (PoolsScene.cs:1048-1049). The crock's water is a disc the game draws itself. And the sheet's style is fixed before the finish is chosen.
problems.fix: Ask for no glow and no water. Run it in stage 2b, in the winning finish.

problems.problem: The quadrants of a 2x2 sheet won't tile; they need the courtyard_textures.py post-pass anyway. 'Mineral sparkle' and 'fine crystals' can't survive two toon bands. problems.problem: The sightline is impossible: a 1.4 x 1.6 m mouth at the end of a tunnel at least 3.6 m long shows a bright slot, not the footbridge, lamp post, portcullis teeth, falls and trunk. To fit them in, Nano will enlarge the mouth, which defeats the test. 'Unlit' contradicts pools.py (the lamp is lit once the pools open, and the player is inside) and the night shot's lit lamp. The brook flows into the grotto, toward the viewer, not 'running away'. corner-a shows neither the water-gate arch nor the portcullis. The master already shows the mouth at game scale.

problems.problem: There is no check of candidates against the HUD before picking a master or a finish, although the layout argument rests on clearances.

problems.problem: Its style reference (night-a) differs from the tended shot's (keyframe A), so stage 2 mixes house styles. Rooms ignore the clock today, so this frame explores a feature that doesn't exist yet.

problems.problem: It shows what the game camera never will. It helps only as key art and for open question 3 (what is seen through the oculus), and could sell the designer a view the game doesn't deliver.

problems.problem: The text-rewrite list misses more prose that ties the Sunward to the falls. Sun-Grit: 'Warm golden grit from under the falls'. Its silt find: 'the falls have been dropping here for years'. Silver Silt: 'the falls used to carry'.

problems.problem: The whole of stage 2 assumes the shared camera. Under it, the oculus (the hero of all three chosen images) and the 'quiet awe' of looking up are never visible in game. That sits buried among the open questions.

missing_shots: Focus-camera frame: what the player sees while working. Target = subject - right*2.35, distance 11.2, left 40% kept plain for the card. Frame the top pool and the druids' bag. It shows the room's right side out to x of about 8, past the current kit's 5.6 edge, and whether the near lip hides laid objects and soak rings at that angle. Build-honest finish: the master as this renderer would actually draw it, with two flat light bands, an even inverted-hull ink outline on every mesh, no cast shadows, no reflections, flat oval water with a fresnel rim, and particle steam. It sets what the engine can build beside the aspirational finishes. 2 x 2K.
0 credits: a to-scale plan and section drawn from the tested layout and the HubCity constants (courtyard 0, scarp shelf -1, wall x 12.9-16.5), plus a HUD-overlay pass on every candidate image.
The Sunward steaming inside the noon beam (the Sun-Lens state, Light 5 / Heat 2), the likeliest mid-game sight and the case the GPT concept lost. Fold it into states-room-tended.
The starting plants and snails: Hush-Moss along the Shade bed, the Lantern Reed's glowing tip, butter-shelled Yellow-backed Snails on the bed (not the rims). Fold them into the creature sheet.
Optional: one master variant with the brief's top -> middle -> bottom cascade, so the designer sees the water-route open question at the game camera rather than only the runnel bypass.

view-threshold as written (2 cr): the sightline through a 1.4 x 1.6 m mouth at the end of a tunnel at least 3.6 m long is impossible. The lamp state and brook direction are wrong, and corner-a has no arch or portcullis. The master already shows the mouth at game scale.
view-section's second variant (2 cr): at most one render, made only after a to-scale section has settled the tunnel descent and where the oculus is.
